packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-16: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure and process statement
- No identification or reading of this fragment reached me from outside the images. The only identifying text I saw is modern pencil on the parchment: "Stams, STA, Frg. 134r" (image-012/013, face A) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 134v" (image-026, face B), plus a modern pencil note on face A (see below). I did not identify the work or author.
- I viewed all 26 images. Some first attempts returned no image ("media removed"); I re-opened those and every image was viewed. Nothing else was opened (packet.json was not read).

Conventions
- Lines are text lines (staves not counted), numbered from the top of the page or column as visible in the overview. Each line cites the tile(s) where it is read. Tiles overlap, and repeats are not counted.
- [red] = rubric ink. Expansions in (); "?" = uncertain; [illegible] = could not read.

==================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observation only)
==================================================================
- One bifolium (two leaves joined at a fold with sewing holes), photographed open on each face. One column per page.
- Each page has 8 text lines, each under a red four-line staff with black neumes (Gothic/hufnagel-type note shapes). Letter clefs c and f stand at the left of the staves. A text line followed by a blank lower margin ends each page, so the foot of the page survives. The top line on each page is partly cut by damage.
- Red initials begin each strophe (S, T, L, G, I, Q, X, B). One large painted/decorated red initial with a pen-flourished tail (face A, left page, line 8). Red rubrics give service headings: "ad t(er)ciam ymnus", "De virginib(us)", "In dedicatione", and in the margin "ad p[...]".
- Face B left page: the staves under lines 5-7 carry a second set of rhombic notes with stems, in a different and paler style that looks like a later addition. Show-through or offset of staves and notes is visible in the lower margins.
- Modern pencil, face A right page, below the text: "Aus IV/77", "Obtel.? [illegible]" and "1663/84", plus the shelfmark noted above.
- Tentative interpretation (not identification): strophic texts (hymn-like, short lines with doxology endings) with music, grouped under liturgical headings. I do not infer date, work or origin.
- Selection: I read every text line on both faces. Weak areas are listed under Limitations.

==================================================================
FACE A ("134r"; overview 001)
==================================================================
--- Left page (tiles 002, 003, 006, 007, 010, 011) ---
1 (002/003)  consors paterni luminis [red S][black] anguis xp(ist)i? fus[...]?   (end of line damaged by tear/abrasion)
2 (002/003)  peremptor hostis invidi fac sitire da venire ad
3 (002/003)  cenam agni providi [red T][black] ue genti recolenti tue co
4 (006/007)  [co]?rone supplicium da virtutem et salutem xp(ist)e
5 (006/007)  redemptor omnium [red L][black] aus honor virtus gloria
6 (006/007)  deo patri et filio sancto simul paraclyto in sem
7 (010/011)  piterna secula amen [red] ad t(er)ciam ymnus
8 (010/011)  [large decorated red initial, probably I][black] esu? velatus facie fuisti sol iusticie flexis illu   (small black letter before "esu", unclear)
   [blank lower margin follows]

--- Right page (tiles 004, 005, 008, 009, 012, 013) ---
1 (004/005)  con[illegible]? letemur [illegible] p(e)c(c)atum? macte? polo   (top line abraded, read with low confidence)
2 (004/005)  [p]atris. [red G][black] loria tibi d(omi)ne. [red] De virginib(us)

8 (012/013)  [red flourished Q][black] uocu(m)q(ue) pergis virgines sequuntur
   [blank lower margin with the modern pencil notes]

==================================================================

2 (017/018)  gloria unigenito una cu(m) s(an)c(t)o sp(irit)u in sempiterna s(e)c(u)la am(en).
3 (017/018)  [red B][black] eata [illegible, abraded ~8 letters; small hole] xp(ist)i passio sit nostra libe   [margin, red: "ad p[ri]?m[am]?" (reads "adp" + superscript)]
4 (021/022)  ratio ut per hanc nobis gaudia sint parata ce
5 (021/022)  lestia. [red Q][black] ui pressura mortis dura solvisti nex
6 (021/022)  us criminum nos ad pacem duc veracem ihesu
7 (025/026)  corona virginum [red I][black] n amara crucis ara fu
8 (025/026)  disti rivos sanguinis ihesu digne rex benigne
   [one more empty staff below, then blank lower margin and pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 134v"]

==================================================================
LIMITATIONS
==================================================================
- The first text line of every page is damaged by the torn or abraded top edge. Readings there are weak: face A left line 1 ending, face A right line 1 (most of it), face B left line 1 ending, and face B right line 1 opening.
- Face B right line 3 has an abraded gap after "Beata". The red marginal rubric there is uncertain.
- Face A right line 7: the red rubric is partly in a hole.
- Face A left line 8: the large initial's letter form is uncertain (probably I).
- Text from the preceding and following leaves is missing. Each page opens and closes mid-strophe.
- Expansions are my own proposals.
This is an unverified image reading.
